title: Watson Brake mounds
summary: Hunter-gatherers build eleven earth mounds in an oval, joined by ridges. It is considered the oldest earthwork mound complex in North America.
why: Showed that hunter-gatherers, not only later farming societies, could organise large building projects.

notes.problem: Summary drops the source's hedge: 'Watson Brake is considered the oldest earthwork mound complex in North America.'
Source does not say it 'overturned' a farmers-only idea; it says it changed views of what such groups could build.

superlativeSource: considered the oldest earthwork mound complex in North America
